doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Club dates today and the wedding concert in Sweden
summary: Ries rarely gets club-date calls now, but tells of a wedding concert in Sweden with friends from several countries.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you still get called for a club date? Like oh we need some background jazz for a cocktail party? You still get those calls and do you take them?

Not so much anymore. Once in a great while I’ll — if I’m — I was on a flight once going from Sweden back to the U.S. and this lady was sitting next to me who turns out to be a really famous photographer and her thing was doing these lions, a pride of lions in Africa that she had followed for many years. And we had an interesting conversation and she was going to get married and she wanted me to fly to Africa for the wedding and play with my East Gipsy band from Budapest in Africa. I’m like wow that sounds interesting, I’ve never been to Africa, why not? As it turns out they couldn’t make it and so anyway

the wedding then became in Sweden. And then she said, “Well instead of your East Gipsy band, can you bring” she goes, “the theme of our wedding is actually Italian music, like an Italian theme” she goes, “and actually specifically Sicilian.” I said, “Well I actually have friends that have a Sicilian jazz band” I said, “I could bring them.” She goes, “Wow.” And then it turns out like, ‘cause I have all these good friends, in Toronto, Detroit, and Sicily and so we all met in Sweden to play this gig. So Detroit, Toronto, New York, Sicily, meet in Sweden to play this concert. So it was like for a wedding but like really kind of a concert in the restaurant where the wedding was. It was really cool. So those kind of things I will take.
Yeah I guess I was thinking more like the Elks Club in Passaic, New Jersey. That’s some club date.
Yeah it was very cool. So the Elks Club not so much, but I did those as a kid with my dad’s band.
